notes: The DS-ECO-6 corpus line ('nothing organised behind it') is the exact phrasing the brief lists as REFUSED on a town whose rows seat a street gang and front businesses, and this town seats both. The corpus claim and the contradiction table point opposite ways; I kept the 'minor / never grew' half of the claim and dropped the 'nothing organised' half rather than ship a refused line.

Several corpus lines break the brief's own bars: a colon in DS-ECO-1, a semicolon in DS-GEN-18, and 'you will be given' in DS-ECO-12's income spine (a future indicative plus an address to the reader). The brief says not to imitate a breach, so I re-cut all three, but a fallback line that would be dropped by the instruments is an odd thing to be handed as the claim.

The rule 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is unusable where every listed field is UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18) or is a schema path whose 'own word' has no plain-English form (incomeSources.reduce, economicState). I wrote single sentences there, which may be thinner than intended.
DS-ECO-12's income key says 'two or three sources between them' while the field it reads says incomeSources.length = 10. I wrote to neither number, but the key and the field appear to disagree.

The DS-ECO-6 pool is marked dm-only with the note 'the unit itself is the notebook and still rides in spine', while the per-pool notebook instruction says 'none, return an empty list'. I returned an empty notebook and wrote the spine in the notebook register, but the two lines read as if they could also mean one notebook row.

Two stance tags in turn.md ("threshold" for PRESSURED, "counterforce" for TIER: minor shadow activity) are not among the three stances brief.md documents (ledger/street/visitor), so their intended phrasing effect had to be inferred rather than read off a rule.

The STALLED pool's corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which THE MECHANICAL BARS forbid outright; brief.md says not to imitate a breach in the corpus line, so I rewrote the claim as two sentences rather than copying it verbatim, but the exact seam the archiver intended for that split isn't specified.

For the TIER: minor shadow activity pool (dm-only), turn.md instructs the private note to ride in `spine` with `notebook` left empty, overriding brief's general audience==dm rule that would otherwise route dm-only content through `notebook`; the brief never states this per-pool override exists, only the general rule.

PRESSURED's instruction ("write ONE sentence and no second" because no fields are recorded) conflicts in spirit with its own two-sentence corpus fallback line; it's unclear whether that one-sentence cap is meant to bind only a freshly written spine or also the fallback if the unit were dropped.

Several fields are given as concrete FROZEN/LIVE numbers (e.g. blackMarketCapture=8, incomeSources.length=10) that floor 2's no-digit/no-count bar forbids restating, alongside other fields marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD; turn.md doesn't say how much magnitude (e.g. "minor" vs "severe") may be implied in words versus left fully unstated, so I took the minimal reading and named only the field's concept, not its scale.

The MARKET-OPEN corpus line (DS-GEN-13) is itself an ORIGIN — carts stopping before stalls, the town growing around the habit — which the brief names as an outright refusal, and it also carries a semicolon. The brief says the corpus line is the claim to keep but is 'not a model of the law', so I kept only the standing part (the market is open) and dropped the founding. Which half counts as 'the claim' is genuinely ambiguous.

Two pools on one page assert opposite things about the road: DS-GEN-5 'the town takes very little from it' and DS-GEN-6 'the road is a condition of it'. The only instruction is 'write to the pool key', so I wrote both, but as rendered they read as a contradiction. Same shape, milder, between prosperity Comfortable/Prosperous and foodSecurity Pressured.

Nearly every pool's fields are 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD', while the rule that a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it makes a second sentence effectively impossible. Every unit is therefore one sentence, which pushes the whole page onto a single shape — the collapse PART III calls DULL. Unclear whether an unreadable field can ever carry a second sentence.

The stance tags do not all resolve against this town: DS-GEN-13 is stance 'elder' but 'elders' is not in the town's sources list, and 'counterforce' (DS-GEN-5) and 'unfolding' (DS-GEN-2) appear nowhere in the brief's three old stances. With faces at zero the spine is bare so nothing broke, but a stance naming an unseated source would be unusable if a face were asked for.

Audience is dm, yet every pool says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.', so the dm page renders identically to the player page despite the brief's DM REGISTER section. I followed the per-pool instruction. Separately, the pool key 'defenseProfile.readiness.label: Well-Defended' supplies a POSTURE BADGE word as the readiness value while the brief forbids naming the badge word; I wrote to the walls-and-watch rows and never used the word.

Several stance tags on these pools (elder, unfolding, counterforce, "ledger · marks deficit") are not among the three stances brief.md actually defines (ledger/street/visitor), and STANCE says the spine is always bare regardless — unclear what, if anything, these extra tags should change about the bare spine's voice.

Most pools' only listed fields are raw engine paths (axis, readings.scores, readings.viable, etc.) marked UNREADABLE; the rule says a second sentence must "name [the field] in its own word" but naming the field at all risks the raw-identifier bar, so a lawful second sentence looks structurally unreachable on nearly every GEN-3 pool — I defaulted to one sentence throughout rather than guess at a paraphrase.

MARKET-OPEN's own corpus fallback ("carts stopped... {settlement} grew around the habit") reads as exactly the ORIGIN-stated-as-record example brief.md lists as refused, and it also names {settlement} twice and uses a semicolon — the ship-ready fallback for this pool appears to violate the pack's own floor and unit-cap rules.

brief.md says a pool with nothing lawful to write is simply omitted (the hand corpus fills it downstream), but the turn/task requires one unit per listed pool with no omission path; several corpus lines break a mechanical bar (semicolon, colon, which-clause, not-X-but-Y, double "will") or ruling 34/42's veto list, and it's unclear whether the intended behavior is a free rewrite (what I did) or verbatim copy of the flawed line since ruling 40/42 nominally forbid imitating the breach either way.

"THE ORDER: ... keep the move order V1 — PRESENT (the state key alone)" is never defined beyond that one phrase, and the "eight closed level-1 orders" it's contrasted against are never listed, so there is no way to confirm a rewritten spine actually preserves the intended order shape versus merely being in present tense.

Two seats have no roster on this town: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War' face 0 is seated on `elders` and DS-DEF-2 'Internal Security' face 5 / 'Economic Survival' face 1 on `garrison`, and neither source appears in the town block's `roles` or `sources`. I applied the copy-the-corpus-verbatim rule at those seats, which means the elders face ships with unresolved `{elders}` and `{v:take}` tokens in it, in a pool whose declared slot list is '(none)'. The verbatim rule and the slot rule contradict each other there, and I could not satisfy both.

Pool 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' declares 'slots you may use: (none)' and then immediately prints a fill for `{court}`. I treated that as the court face's licensed role wording rather than as a usable token, but which of the two lines governs is genuinely ambiguous.

The block DS-DEF-3 pool key is 'First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)', which is a statement ABOUT the document; ruling 40 and the E2 ratchet forbid the fair copy from naming the survey, the record or this office. I wrote the qualification without any self-reference, but the pool key seems to be asking for exactly the thing the law bars.

Several corpus lines given as 'the claim you must keep' name bodies this card does not carry: 'the muster behind it is thinning' (WALLED-STRAINED) and 'the garrison's' (Internal Security), while forceBuckets has militia false and garrison false and no muster holder resolves. I kept the underlying claim (walls sound, upkeep strained) and moved the strain onto the purse, since naming the muster would breach the every-body-is-a-row bar.

The role roster itself carries words ruling 42c withdrew: 'a guild factor' and 'a pedlar' are offered as seatable roles but are named in the brief as archaisms to replace with 'a guild member' and 'a travelling trader'. I avoided both and picked other roster entries, but the card and the ruling disagree. Separately, the 'second sentence must rest on a listed field' rule has no satisfiable form for 'arcane defense PRESENT', whose only field is UNREADABLE, so I wrote a single sentence.
The turn lists ten pools; DS-POW-7 "layer DORMANT" is marked not writeable and was omitted, so nine units are returned in the turn's own order with blockId, poolKey and vid copied verbatim.

On "riskLabel: Holding" the {seat} and {faction} fills are the SAME string ("Guild Council"), so the corpus claim "holds because {faction} is still the heavier of the two" renders as the body outweighing itself. The claim was kept by naming the body once and leaving the other interest unnamed.

The V5 order (INSTITUTION then PRESENT) plus a single seat fill forces three of the nine spines to open on the same institution name, which collides with the no-repeated-opener guidance. The order was treated as the binding instruction and the opener repetition accepted.

"recentConflict present" is the only pool with readable field values, and it is unclear whether a second sentence is licensed there at all: every other pool says "write ONE sentence and no second" while this one only says a second sentence must rest on a listed field and "name it in its own word" (unclear whether that means the field path or the field's own vocabulary). A second sentence drawn from the FROZEN recentConflict text was written on the vocabulary reading; the frozen value also permits the "have stopped" durative under ruling 11.

Audience is dm, yet every pool declares "notebook: none", so the dm page carries no private rows and the whole notebook register of the brief is unexercised. Separately, two corpus fallback lines contain semicolons, which the mechanical bars forbid; those were read as breaches not to imitate, and the legitimacyHold field is printed as a raw JS expression marked UNREADABLE, so it was treated as no field.

The {institution} fill is "Cartographer's guild", but the town block carries no guild row and no guild source at all (its nearest row is "Cartographer's workshop"). The fill was printed as the card instructed, though it sits against the bar that every body named must be a row this card carries.

The corpus fallback for STALLED breaks two of the brief's own mechanical bars (a semicolon, and "the books" as a generic record). The claim was kept and the breach not imitated, per the corpus line's stated standing.

Four pools list only fields marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD, yet the rule says a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it in its own word. That makes a second sentence unwritable there, so those units were written as one sentence; whether a second sentence resting on the pool key itself is permitted is unclear.

The page is audience dm, but every pool says "notebook: none. Return an empty list." A dm page with no private rows anywhere may be intended, but the brief's DM REGISTER section implies otherwise, and nothing says which wins.

Each pool gives a stance (visitor, ledger, street) and simultaneously "faces to write: 0", so only the bare spine ships. Ruling 40 says a recorded fact stands bare in the archiver's hand, which leaves it unclear what the stance tag is supposed to change in a unit that has no faces.

DS-POW-4 riskLabel Holding: card fills both {seat} and {faction} with the identical value Guild Council, so the corpus claim (holds because the faction is still the heavier of the two) compares the seat to itself; there is no second party for the two to name, so I wrote the comparison as no rival faction outweighs it rather than repeat the same name twice.

DS-POW-2 recentConflict present: the FROZEN field text spells out a duration (three months) and the fair-copy floor bars stating a count as record while ruling 11 licenses durative language only over frozen fields; the interaction was not resolved in the brief, so I grounded the second sentence in the field's content (the levy dispute, the merchants withdrawing) without repeating the duration, to stay on the safe side.

DS-POW-4 legitimacyHold: the listed field is a raw ternary expression (typeof power.publicLegitimacy...) rather than a named value, and its state is UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD; it is unclear how a second sentence could ever name it in its own word, so I wrote one sentence only, matching the fallback's own choice.

Two of the given corpus fallback lines break the brief's own mechanical bars (the PROSPERITY favourable line ends on a which-clause close the brief separately flags as a breach not to imitate, and the recentConflict line contains a semicolon, which is an outright mechanical bar); the turn is right to warn against imitating the breach, but it means the line that ships if a render is refused is itself non-compliant with the bars it enforces.

DS-POW-6 operation role money laundering: the given corpus line cites the books of several houses as a generic record, which THE VOICE section explicitly forbids (never the books as a generic); I rewrote around it (houses that show nothing amiss) rather than imitate the breach.

ROLE ROSTER vs SEATED SOURCES: the turn asks for faces through watch, court, guild, hall, gate, muster and garrison, but the town block's `sources` and `roles` seat only elders, market, public, register, stranger and tavern, and forceBuckets sets garrison/militia/watch to false. Those seats have no lawful role phrase, so I applied the brief's 'WHEN THE CARD GIVES A FACE NOTHING TO STAND ON, COPY THE CORPUS' rule and reproduced the corpus row verbatim at each (4 in Invasion & War, 2 in Internal Security, 4 in Economic Survival). It is unclear whether the harness intends that, or whether the turn's seating is a card/roster mismatch.

42c vs THE SEATED ROLES: the VOICE section strikes 'alehouse' and 'pedlar' as archaic words that do not survive, yet the town's own tavern and stranger rosters are literally 'a carter at the alehouse', 'the drinkers at the alehouse' and 'a pedlar', and a mechanical bar requires every role phrase to be one the town seats. I avoided 'a pedlar' entirely and used the two alehouse roles only after the two non-alehouse tavern roles were spent across four pools. Which rule wins is not stated.

A COPIED CORPUS ROW CAN CONTRADICT THE SPINE I AM TOLD TO WRITE: Economic Survival face 8 is 'Nobody here asks the soldiers their business, the soldiers say...', which asserts soldiers on a town whose force buckets are all false and whose Invasion & War key is 'neither walls nor force'. The brief says a copied corpus row is never refused, so I copied it, but the page now carries two readings that cannot both hold.

THE 'FIRST-SURVEY QUALIFICATION' POOL ASKS FOR THE ONE THING RULING 40 BARS: its whole subject is that the reading is a first look, while ruling 40 and the E2 ratchet refuse 'the survey', 'the record' and 'this office' on a player face and exempt only the notebook, which this card holds at zero rows. I wrote 'The safety reading here is a first look' on the reading that a named page badge is not the document citing itself; if the ratchet greps more broadly this unit will drop.

SECOND-SENTENCE RULE AND THE UNREADABLE FIELDS: 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is hard to satisfy where the only field is `institutions = [29 rows]` (which word counts as naming it?) or where the field is UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD and I may assert no value for it. I kept those spines to one sentence to stay clear of the rule. Also unclear: whether the three-sentence unit cap counts the spine plus one drawn face, or the spine plus all nine written faces.

turn.md's fill for {institution} in DS-GEN-18 is "Cartographer's guild", but town.md's institution roster lists "Cartographer's workshop" (no "guild" entry) -- wrote the fill as instructed (WRITE THE FILL, NOT THE TOKEN) but the two files disagree on the institution's name.

Several pools' only listed readable field is itself marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (DS-ECO-1's prosperityRank, DS-ECO-10's exportPosture.status, all of DS-GEN-18's readings fields), while the brief requires any second sentence to 'rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' -- unclear how to ground a sentence in a field whose value is explicitly withheld versus just gesturing at its subject matter.

DS-GEN-18's own corpus fallback line uses a semicolon and cites a bare 'the books' -- both forms the brief elsewhere calls hard bars / explicitly-refused generics -- and DS-ECO-1's corpus line uses a colon, which PART V of the brief reserves for the notebook register only, not the fair copy; the brief says not to imitate a corpus breach, so I rewrote around all three, but the shipped fallback itself would not pass its own rules.

Hochhausen's town.md roster (sources: elders, market, public, register, stranger, tavern) has no 'hall' or 'guild' speaking role at all, though brief.md's worked exemplars lean heavily on hall/guild attribution -- irrelevant to this render since every pool here has faces:0, but would bind hard on any future face-writing for this town.

turn.md's page-level state block (advanced/calendar/tick/renderYear/renderYearIsFrozen/foodStockpileLastTick) is given as 'THE STATE THIS PAGE READS' but none of the six pools' own per-pool field lists reference any of it, so its intended bearing on this particular render is unclear.
